signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: CHF outperforms across the G10 with a 1W average of +1.226% across 6 pairs, while AUD lags at -2.242% across 4 pairs, creating an extreme 3.467% spread. Multiple naval mine explosions east of the Strait of Hormuz involving commercial tankers have triggered acute maritime security stress and driven flight-to-safety flows into CHF. This geopolitical shock overrides the underlying rate structure, where RBA at 4.85% vs SNB at 0.00% offers a 485bp nominal carry advantage to AUD. AUD/CHF trades at 0.56270, well below its fair value model estimate of 0.5753 (z=-3.27σ), reflecting intense cross-asset liquidation. Elevated risk sentiment across global markets accelerates the compression of high-beta carry crosses. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF, momentum favors safe-haven CHF over high-beta AUD during acute corridor disruption. Catalyst: RBA meeting 8 Dec — hike bias priced. Risk: Geopolitical de-escalation along the Strait transit route spurs a violent mean-reversion squeeze toward 0.5750.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Elevated Vol Premium + Intervention Watch
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.28, holding below its SMA200 at 158.56 while remaining above the SMA20 and SMA50 at 157.96 and 157.30. Saxo 1M ATM implied volatility sits at 6.9% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.8%, generating an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +2.0%. Concurrently, the 25-delta risk reversal prints at -1.97, reflecting substantial institutional put skew and aggressive downside hedging demand. A 269bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.92% vs TONA 1.23%) continues to anchor the long-term dollar bid against negative real Japanese policy rates of -2.25%. However, with spot trading near multi-month highs, 160.00 remains the key level that has previously triggered Ministry of Finance warnings and intervention concerns. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported while holding above 157.96 SMA20. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions release at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Spot prints a sustained break above 160.00, prompting direct official intervention.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short vs Retail Extreme
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1151, trapped in a clear downtrend beneath its descending SMA20 at 1.1195, SMA50 at 1.1347, and SMA200 at 1.1550. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds hold an extreme net short of -104,030 contracts, placing positioning at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range (z=-1.80σ) after adding 4,473 contracts of shorts WoW. In direct contrast, Retail sentiment data retail sentiment registers an extreme 85% long bias, setting up sharp institutional-versus-retail divergence. Macro carry structurally suppresses euro upside, with Fed at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% delivering a 135bp policy rate advantage to the dollar, corroborated by a 148bp SOFR-€STR spread. Furthermore, US 5Y yields rose +2bp in real terms over 5D according to FRED data, maintaining underlying support for the greenback. Trade bias: Short EUR/USD, institutional short trend and rate differentials outweigh retail contrarian positioning. Catalyst: US CPI release on 10 Nov — forecast 4.2% y/y. Risk: Leveraged funds trigger an abrupt short-squeeze covering rally above 1.1200 on an inflation miss.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Real-Yield Repricing + Technical Breakout
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4119, breaking decisively above its technical cluster with the close above the SMA20 at 1.4069, SMA50 at 1.4043, and SMA200 at 1.3890. The move follows divergent labor dynamics, where Canadian unemployment rose to 6.7% (a 3.00σ negative surprise) while US employment prints remain robust. Fed at 4.00% vs BoC at 2.50% maintains a 150bp nominal rate spread favoring the dollar, reinforced by a 140bp SOFR vs CORRA OIS differential. In options markets, 1M 25d risk reversals sit flat at +0.08, showing no meaningful options hedge against further upside expansion. The underlying US yield decomposition shows nominal 5Y yields at 4.59% with real yields at 2.33% (FRED, as of Nov 5), maintaining structural rate support. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD, macro growth and policy divergence favor further topside discovery. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Dec — 100% hike priced. Risk: WTI crude prices rebound sharply above $95.0/bbl, restoring CAD terms-of-trade support.
